key: Agni bestows all vital power even as each man supplicates. He brings the Vasus strengthening gifts, and grants delight, in rest and stir, for every calling on the Gods.
s: A hymn to Agni, each verse wishing all the others away, praises him as the gods’ messenger; Sāyaṇa, commentary on 8.39.4, reads the delight as happiness born of calm and of the senses’ objects, and takes Agni as doing all, whichever god is invoked.

evidence.words: “ऊर्जाहुतिः अन्नेनाहूयमानोऽग्निः “वसूनां हविषां वासकानां यजमानानां “शं शान्तिनिमित्तं "योः विषययोगजनितं “च “मयः सुखं “दधे करोति । “विश्वस्यै “देवहूत्यै सर्वस्मै देवानां ह्वानाय च भवति । यः कश्चनापि देवो यदि हूयते अग्निरेव सर्वं करोतीत्यर्थः ।
evidence.gloss: Agni, invoked with food (ūrjāhutiḥ), makes (dadhe) for the Vasus, that is the sacrificers who hold the oblations, happiness (mayaḥ), both śam, caused by tranquillity, and yoḥ, born of contact with the objects of sense. He is there for every invocation of the gods: whatever god is invoked, Agni alone does everything; that is the meaning.

reason: Key verse verbatim (verse.js ok, 8.39.4 at [658,4]); the packet’s Sanskrit (tat-tad agnir vayo dadhe ... śaṃ ca yoś ca mayo dadhe viśvasyai devahūtyai) is the app’s verse. Sāyaṇa glosses śam as śāntinimittam and yoḥ as viṣayayogajanitam, qualifying mayaḥ sukham, and explains viśvasyai devahūtyai as: whatever god is invoked, Agni alone does all. Both halves of the reading are his words; Wilson’s note confirms the first as Sāyaṇa’s interpretation. Plain sense faithful: every verse of 8.39 ends with the refrain that all the others die away, and 8.39.1 and 3 call Agni the messenger; no four-word run from the key.
